Done. All checks pass. Summary of the change:

**Migration** — `db/migrations/003_raise_estimate_limit_to_60.sql` (new file; applied migrations 001–002 untouched). SQLite can't alter a check constraint in place, so it rebuilds `tasks` with `estimate_hours between 1 and 60`, copying existing rows (including `id` and `created_at`) across. Verified on a fresh DB via `npm run db:reset` + replay: 60 is accepted, 61 is rejected at the SQL level, existing data (e.g. a 40h task) survives.

**Code** — `lib/tasks.ts:20-22`: validation range is now `1..60` and the error message says `estimateHours must be 1..60`. `app/api/tasks/route.ts` needed no change (it delegates to `createTask`, still answering 422 on `RuleViolation`).

**Tests** — `lib/tasks.test.ts` (TDD): added a test accepting `estimateHours: 60` (watched it fail first against the old 1..40 rule) and one rejecting 61. Suite: 6/6 passing.

**Docs** — README's business-rules table updated to `estimate 1..60 h`. I left `docs/tickets/TASK-7.md` and the CI/trailer templates alone — those are records of the earlier whole-hours ticket, not live rules.

**Checks** — `npm test` ✅ 6 passed · `npm run typecheck` ✅ · `npm run db:reset` ✅ · `git status` shows no modification to applied migrations, only the new `003_*.sql`.

Rollback note (for the eventual PR): rolling back this migration means existing rows keep `estimate_hours` as stored; the column itself and any values above 40 remain in the DB, and code at the old revision would stop enforcing the wider range only at its 1..40 check. SQLite rebuilds the table, so no data is dropped — re-applying 001–002 alone is not possible on a database that has 003 applied.

Changes are uncommitted in this worktree — say the word if you want them committed (and per the homework's gate, the commit would take `Refs:`/`Evidence:` trailers).
